clue.text: Unruffled church leader wearing tartan cloth

indicators.note: the tartan cloth wears the church leader, so it is placed round that letter

parts.note: a plaid is a length of tartan cloth worn in Scottish dress

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of church

explanation.surface: A calm minister sits wrapped in a tartan blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone placid is calm and not easily disturbed, a plain synonym for unruffled.

clue.text: Card-game in Paris that's eclipsed by mine

indicators.note: to be eclipsed is to be covered over, so the mine goes round the French word

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
que is French for that

explanation.surface: A card game played in Paris is overshadowed by a mining operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquet is an old two-player card game played with a short pack of 32 cards.

clue.text: Change of tack with regard to revolution

parts.note: about means concerning, with regard to
a turn is one revolution, as of a wheel

explanation.surface: A sailor's change of course is described in terms of rotating.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-turn is a complete reversal of policy or direction, a change of tack in figurative terms.

clue.text: Man using current account to cover appeal

indicators.note: the current and account letters go over and around the appeal

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone uses the money in their bank account to fund a legal appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a man's name, the Biblical son of Abraham, so it is an example of a man.

clue.text: Stocky bumpkins in first part of trashy film

indicators.note: the bumpkins sit inside the letters formed by the rest of the clue
the first part of trashy is its opening letter

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an alien
hicks are unsophisticated country people

explanation.surface: Burly country yokels appear at the start of a low-grade movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset describes a heavily built, solid body, the same as stocky.

clue.text: Suspended Irishman in father's toothless legislature?

parts.note: hung means suspended, as from a hook

indicators.note: the Irishman is placed inside the word for father

parts.note: a father is a parent; the possessive just links
Liam is a typical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: An Irishman is strung up within his father's feeble governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: When no party has a majority, the assembly struggles to pass laws, so it is a legislature without bite; the question mark flags the playful description.

clue.text: Time to leave street party — it's getting noisier!

indicators.note: the time letter leaves the street name, so it is taken out

parts.note: a crescent is a curved street
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Time to quit a street party, because the noise keeps rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes T out of CRESCENT, giving CRESCEN.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness, a passage growing louder.

clue.text: Social misfit theologian introduced to Portuguese saint

indicators.note: the theologian is put inside the Portuguese title

parts.note: Sao is the Portuguese word for saint, as in Sao Paulo
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian

explanation.surface: An awkward loner who studies religion meets a Portuguese holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddo is British slang for a pathetic, socially inadequate person.

clue.text: Employing son for second time, strangle singer

indicators.note: employing the son means using it in the word
the son goes in for, in place of, the second time letter

parts.note: to throttle is to strangle
the second T in the word for strangle, T being short for time

explanation.surface: Someone using their son a second time throttles a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A throstle is an old or poetic name for the song thrush, a singing bird.

clue.text: Quiet agreement at home about old instrument

parts.note: piano is the musical direction for quiet
an accord is an agreement

indicators.note: the at-home word goes about, around, the old letter

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A quiet agreement reached at home over an old instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano accordion is a squeezebox with a piano-style keyboard, a musical instrument.

clue.text: Estimated cost of passage from St Paul, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a builder's quote, a written price in advance
a cited extract from a writer, such as the Epistles

explanation.definitionFit: A quotation is both a price offered for a job and an extract cited from a text, here from the apostle's letters.

clue.text: More senior lord received by English queen

indicators.note: the lord is taken in by the English queen, so goes inside

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen

explanation.surface: An older nobleman is given an audience by the English monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Elder means older or of higher seniority, comparative of old.

clue.text: Aquatic amphibian moved away, missing lake

indicators.note: the word for moved away is missing the lake letter

parts.note: left means departed, moved away

explanation.surface: A water creature has quit its home, there being no lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, a small amphibian that lives in water.

clue.text: Glaring politician's photo initially unwanted round America

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative politician; with the possessive it gives CONS
a pic is a photo

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of unwanted

parts.note: O is round in shape
US is America

explanation.surface: A politician's unwelcome photograph circulates glaringly around America.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaring and conspicuous both mean obvious and impossible to miss.

clue.text: A way teachers recalled a cold, treeless zone

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: RD, road, is a way
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union

explanation.surface: Teachers remember a route through a frozen landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast flat Arctic region where the subsoil is frozen and no trees grow.

clue.text: Repudiation doctor said I for example talked of?

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of said are rearranged
spoken of, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: I is an example of a vowel

explanation.surface: A doctor's remark about himself being the subject of conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' rearranges SAID into DISA; 'talked of' turns VOWEL into the sound-alike VOWAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A disavowal is a denial or rejection of something, the same as a repudiation.

clue.text: Replacement of kidney involving theatre crew ultimately

indicators.note: the kidney word involves, takes inside, the last letters

parts.note: renal means relating to the kidney

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of each of theatre and crew

explanation.surface: A kidney transplant needs the help of the operating theatre team.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewal is the replacing of something worn out with something new.

clue.text: Forest-dweller with sex appeal eclipsing dandy regularly

indicators.note: the sex appeal word covers, goes round, the dandy letters

parts.note: oomph is sex appeal

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters of dandy

explanation.surface: A sexy forest creature outshines a fashionable dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth a dryad or similar nature spirit lives in the trees, an inhabitant of the forest.

clue.text: Musician and detective on island propping up bar

indicators.note: in a down clue the rest stands under the bar word, holding it up

parts.note: to ban is to bar

indicators.note: in a down clue the detective sits on top of the island

parts.note: DS is a Detective Sergeant
the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: A musician and a detective on an island lean against the pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like the pub counter but is the verb meaning to prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandsman is a player in a band, especially a brass or military band.

clue.text: Apt to forget made-up names one coined originally

indicators.note: made-up means invented, so the letters of names are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of coined

explanation.surface: Someone forgetful invents names that one person originally coined.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesic means suffering from memory loss, so prone to forgetting.

clue.text: I work in turfy ground, finding woodlouse, for example

indicators.note: the work letters go inside the turf word

parts.note: sod is turf, ground covered in grass
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A gardener digging the lawn comes across a woodlouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An isopod is a crustacean of the order that includes woodlice, so a woodlouse is one.

clue.text: Inventor displaying lack of arrogance when given rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: no means a lack of, none
side is an old word for swagger or arrogance, as in putting on side

explanation.surface: An inventor shows modesty when he is promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Courier given keys by member of guild

parts.note: D and E are musical keys
a liveryman is a member of a City of London livery company, an old trade guild

explanation.surface: A messenger is handed the keys by a guild member.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier is someone who delivers parcels and messages, a delivery worker.

clue.text: Roles for top players City picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, in northern England

explanation.surface: A football club signs up leading actors for starring parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The lead in a play or film is the principal role, taken by the star performers.

clue.text: Anxious French marshal clutching version of Bible

indicators.note: the marshal holds the version letters inside

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A worried French general grips his copy of the scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervy is British informal for nervous and jumpy, so anxious.

clue.text: Signal agreement? Homer sometimes did

definitions.meaning: to dip the head to show assent
the proverb 'even Homer ...' says even the greatest writer sometimes slips

explanation.definitionFit: Bowing the head shows yes, and the saying about the Greek poet uses the same verb for a lapse in attention.

clue.text: Complaint from queen, perhaps, brought back without purpose?

indicators.note: brought back means the letters run in the reverse order

parts.note: w/o is the written abbreviation for without
an aim is a purpose

explanation.surface: A monarch grumbles at being recalled for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' looks royal but is a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a female cat, and its plaintive cry is the sound of a cat.

clue.text: Dimwit's problem a boy soldier reversed

indicators.note: the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
Ron is a boy's name
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A slow-witted soldier's difficulty is that he has been demoted.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant, stupid person, the same as a dimwit.

clue.text: Young bird in web disturbed by small fish

indicators.note: the web is broken into by the small letter, which goes inside

parts.note: a net is a web of mesh
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A chick caught in a net is troubled by a little fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestling is a baby bird too young to leave its nest.

clue.text: Huggy type not entirely happy — tho nearly

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the answer sits within them

explanation.surface: An affectionate person is not quite cheerful, though almost.
explanation.definitionFit: This snake is a constrictor that squeezes its prey, so it is jokingly a hugger.
